I see you had to add linter ignore for this check in your main file. Is this required for a single-threaded event loop?
We leave these turned on even if there are cases we ignore them.  In main, it's pretty clear that it can't be a multithread issue, because we haven't started any threads yet.
Done
Can we put this at the root?  If not, what's preventing that?

There is already a .clang-tidy at the root.  It doesn't have the c++ checks enabled.  I seem to remember that a lot of common c-idioms get flagged by the c++ checks but I could be mis-remembering.

I'm willing to doing some work here but I think I need a hint as to what it would be.
Marking as resolved, please unresolve as desired.
Several headers missed.
Done
nit: Can this be a `std::unique_ptr`?
Why would that be better if the pointer isn't required?
Semantically, at least for me, unique_ptr made sense. I was coming at it from the thinking that App is the sole owner of Bus, and the bus cannot outlive the app or be accidentally shared.

> and the bus cannot outlive the app or be accidentally shared.

That is the intent but I'm not sure how unique_ptr helps with that?  Please unresolve if there is still a concern.
nit: Maybe name this `file`?
This call throws if the directory doesn't exist for some reason.  Please use the EC overload if we're handling this error at this level.
Open to a better name, but I don't think file is it because an entry could be a directory...
will do.
I reworked slightly to just pass the opened directory iterator from main (and use the ec overload there).
not sure how this snuck in here.
Done
std::from_chars here would avoid needing to throw/catch.
will do.
Done
Can we maybe log an error and continue?

Sorry I'm confused.  We do continue on error; are you saying you'd like to see the continue keyword explicitly?

As far as logging it goes...I guess the scenario would be that someone wrote a file in the state directory?  Or more likely is a developer is running the application locally and the state directory defaulted to $CWD which has the development source files in it?  Do we really want to log all that?  That seems pointlessly noisy to me.  Please unresolve if there are still concerns.
Can this function return `std::error_code` instead of an integer?
nit, could we pass by std::span to avoid the dependency on vector?

using std::error_code in apis that don't use std library things isn't commonly done.  IF we were going to change this, I would recommend we use an enum class for the various return codes that this function can return.

With that said, returning an int for failure is pretty well defined.
Okay, got it. Returning an int for failure felt very C-like, hence the comment.
will do.
Done
Can we set a more specific limit here?  Maybe 20KB?  It's arbitrary, but I'm assuming we don't want to allow writing 4GB to a file.
will do.

will do.

nit: Can this index be incremented in the `writeCper` function?

It could.  Why do you prefer it there?  I tend to prefer putting logic such as this higher in the stack as opposed to lower, to facilitate potential reuse.  Please un-resolve if there are still concerns.
This is meant to be returned directly.

Should this be a full dbus path rather than an index?  I can't see any use for this other than just immediately using it to log, and if you're going to do that you should be using the path.

There is no path in the API/model to return...

I had modeled it like that initially where storing a CPER created a first class D-Bus interface with a read method, but in the docs repository review you had asked for a post-code like interface so that each cper didn't have its own dbus object to save on start up introspection costs.

>  I can't see any use for this other than just immediately using it to log

no need to return 1 here.
